What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

description: Pack of 5 each 6" x 6" Enluxtra wound dressing ENLUXTRA "Any Wound" Functionally Self-Adaptive Dressing is the first and only self-regulating superabsorbent fiber dressing with localized adaptive absorbency and built-in localized adaptive hydration function. ENLUXTRA was developed as a healing tool, with the goal of simplification of confusing dressing selection process, in order to help medical professionals focus on other important wound healing aspects. ENLUXTRA's patented technology continuously monitors and neutralizes the factors that may impede wound healing, cause wound deterioration and further complications. ​ 1 each 4 x 4 dressing: WHAT MAKES ENLUXTRA ONE OF A KIND?​ Wounds are non-uniform and constantly changing objects. By nature every wound has different ever-changing areas that need different dynamically changing care. ENLUXTRA is able to sense the wound's needs and to act in accordance with them. If a wound or even a part of it changes its state while the Self-Adaptive Dressing is on, the dressing will automatically and reversibly change its function locally at this particular area. - If, for some reason, a part of a dry/granulating wound unexpectedly starts exuding, the dressing at this area switches its local function from hydration to absorption, while all other dressing areas continue to hydrate the dry parts of the wound. - If the wound stops exuding, the local function of the dressing reverts back to hydration. With this technology, maceration and desiccation will never occur, thus resulting in a more desirable healing process of any wound in any wound stage. Self-Adaptive Wound Dressing dynamically balances the evolving moist wound environment, providing hydration or absorption locally, depending on the instantaneous needs of wound and peri-wound skin. Dry areas of the wound stay properly hydrated, fluid from exuding areas is absorbed and locked in, and peri-wound skin is protected from maceration. OSNovative Systems, Inc.

bullet_point: [Prevent blisters and hot spots when breaking in new shoes and boots; use for hiking, walking on the job, jogging, and all athletic activities, Thin bubble glides freely to absorb rubbing action and deflect friction away from the skin, Breathable, water-resistant, latex-free for multiday blister protection; includes 4 transparent adhesive bandages, More effective alternative to moleskin, roll-ons, and sprays, Bandages measure 2.6 x 1.5 inches]
description:
Sawyer's ultra-thin, medical grade Blist-O-Ban adhesive bandages provides blister protection and helps stop and prevent footwear hot spots with patented friction and rubbing relief technology.

Designed to help prevent blisters before they start, Blist-O-Ban transparent, breathable, water-resistant, and latex-free adhesive bandages are ideal for use over any blisters, hot spots, or injury prone areas. They’re perfect for breaking in a new pair of boots, going on a hike, heading out for a jog, or working a long walking shift on the job.

The Blist-O-Ban bandage features a patented dome that glides smoothly in all directions, deflecting friction and shear forces away from the skin. When a force is applied to the skin, the central dome collapses and produces a gliding movement, effectively redirecting the pressure vector away from the protected area.

If movement exceeds the distance the dome can glide, the low friction polyurethane material will reduce friction experienced over the affected area. The area under the central dome will also experience less mechanical trauma, providing relief during use.

Since 1984, Sawyer Products has offered the best, most technologically advanced solutions for protection against sun, bugs, water, and injuries -- everything from first aid kits developed for wilderness to point-of-use water filters that filter contaminated water to levels cleaner than U.S. bottled water.

Ideal for Chronic and Acute Wounds

KerraCel Ag Dressings make wound care treatment even better with the added power of Ag Oxysalts to effectively kill 99.999% of bacteria - even within a biofilm. Biofilm, a collection of bacteria and fungi held together by a protective layer, is common in 78% of chronic wounds and is extremely difficult to remove. Biofilm can compromise wound healing and cause chronic inflammatory problems. KerraCel Ag can address the challenges of biofilm due to it's higher solubility which allows more silver to get at and kill bacteria faster.

A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.

description:
Silver Nitrate Sticks are a device containing Silver Nitrate and Potassium Nitrate on its tip.

Silver Nitrate has a bactericidal, astringent, caustic effect. When moistened, it leads to a denaturation (coagulation) of the proteins and subsequent dying off of the treated tissue.
The purpose of using Potassium Nitrate is to mitigate the effect of Silver Nitrate. The users have formed their own preferences and there are no formal recommendations regarding strength, lenght or material.

The tip of the stick should be moistened with water. If there is enough moisture on the area to be treated, it may not be necessary to moisten the stick. The aim is to transfer the water of the tip, rich in Silver Nitrate, to the area being treated. The area should be touched by dabbing and rolling the tip several times, without rubbing or pressing, taking care to use exact precision. The treaded area will discolour and shed off from the surrounding tissue after a few days.

It may take up to 24 hours until the treated area turns black.

Q&A:

Q: Does this stick to skin?
A: No, it sticks to itself so works great on hand, legs and places that you can wrap the bandage around. Plus, it is super easy to remove.

Q: Can I cut this wrap lengthwise for smaller legs, etc. or should I get the thinner wraps?
A: Yes, you can cut this wrap lengthwise if needed. Although if you have smaller legs, having rolls of smaller wrap on hand might not be a bad idea for convenience sake.

Q: Can it be reused?
A: For wounds, we don’t suggest to reuse the wrap due to hygiene reason. If the purpose is use on muscles and joints support, compression and bandage securing you might get a few uses out of it.

Q: Is it waterproof?
A: wrap is NOT waterproof. It is mildly water resistant.

Q: Can this wrap be used like an Ace bandage on my friend to help provide compression and support for some injury-based arthritis?
A: Wrap sticks to itself, but there is stretch to it. We believe using an ace bandage would be better. The wrap is more of a covering (secure) for a bandage. Always talk to your doctor if you are not sure about something.

Q: Can this be used to protect injured family nails?
A: Potentially it could work for protecting nails but you might want to add a protective layer over the top so that the material would last longer.

Q&A:

Q: Does this stick to skin?
A: No, it sticks to itself so works great on hand, legs and places that you can wrap the bandage around. Plus, it is super easy to remove.

Q: Can I cut this wrap lengthwise for smaller legs, etc. or should I get the thinner wraps?
A: Yes, you can cut this wrap lengthwise if needed. Although if you have smaller legs, having rolls of smaller wrap on hand might not be a bad idea for convenience sake.

Q: Can it be reused?
A: For wounds, we don’t suggest to reuse the wrap due to hygiene reason. If the purpose is use on muscles and joints support, compression and bandage securing you might get a few uses out of it.

Q: Is it waterproof?
A: wrap is NOT waterproof. It is mildly water resistant.

Q: Can this wrap be used like an Ace bandage on my friend to help provide compression and support for some injury-based arthritis?
A: Wrap sticks to itself, but there is stretch to it. We believe using an ace bandage would be better. The wrap is more of a covering (secure) for a bandage. Always talk to your doctor if you are not sure about something.

Q: Can this be used to protect injured family nails?
A: Potentially it could work for protecting nails but you might want to add a protective layer over the top so that the material would last longer.

1. Apply pad to the clean and dry skin.

The dressings consist of absorbent polyurethane foam sandwiched between an outer layer of breathable, polyurethane film with adhesive along the borders, and wound-contacting polyethylene net containing silver metal ions (Ag+). The outside film acts as a bacterial barrier, and the silver inhibits microbial growth in the dressing, which helps to prevent colonization. What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.

A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.

description: Hydrofera Blue is a simple, safe, effective and proven moist wound dressing. It is constructed of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) sponge complexed with two organic pigments, which provide broad-spectrum bacteriostatic protection. The pigments (Methylene Blue and Gentian Violet) have been used safely in medicine for over 50 years and have proven effective against a variety of microorganisms including MRSA and VRE. Hydrofera Blue has been approved for use on all types of wounds except third degree burns. Hydrofera Blue is intended for use on complex wounds and, in trials, has shown excellent results in treatment of wounds r/t Pyoderma, radiation burns, chemical burns, venous stasis ulcers, yeast infections, folliculitis and infected wounds. It can also be used to provide a safer moist environment for optimum wound healing on non-infected wounds. Hydrofera Blue is highly absorptive. In addition to being bacteriostatic, its open cell structure provides capillary vacuum action to draw excess fluid and exudates from the wound bed. Hydrofera Blue must be moistened with sterile saline or sterile water, squeezed out and secured to the wound bed with an appropriate secondary dressing. When kept moist, Hydrofera Blue is incredibly soft and comfortable for the patient. Other attributes of the dressing include gentile self-debridement of necrotic tissue and odor control through prevention of the growth of odor causing bacteria on the sponge. Dressings should be changed every 1 to 3 days following good wound care practice. In cases of high infection, the dressing may require more frequent change, which will be indicated by the dressing changing color from blue to white. What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

What's the self-adhering bandage for?

What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

What's the self-adhering bandage for?
1.Great for swelling(medical treatment fixing and wrapping), sprain and general soreness.
2.Widedly Used in Medical, Sports and Veterinary Area.
3.Used to protect the various training, match and sports.
4.Animal medical wrapping and sport protection.
5.To prevent muscle strain.
6.Prepared for the accidential aid kit.

Are You Looking for A Better Way to Stop Bleeding Quick -- So You Can Get Back to Doing What You Want?

AllaQuix is a patented, high-tech gauze pad made of chitosan, which has been used and proven by medical professionals and the US Military to stop bleeding fast.

AllaQuix is a sterile, topical, active hemostatic, wound dressing that is specifically designed to stop bleeding, even for people who normally have trouble stopping bleeding. AllaQuix is designed to stop bleeding – regular gauze and bandage just absorb the blood but don’t actually stop the bleeding.

HOW DOES ALLAQUIX WORK? AllaQuix works independent of the clotting cascade - which means AllaQuix will work whether the body is able to clot blood on its own or not. That makes AllaQuix ideal for people on blood thinners, those who have thin skin or are “bleeders”, or those who have bleeding or clotting disorders, like hemophilia or von Willebrand’s disease.

OPPOSITES ATTRACT! The chitosan fibers in AllaQuix have a positive charge. Red blood cells have a negative charge. Once the AllaQuix gauze is on the wound, the chitosan fibers in AllaQuix attract red blood cells. It’s almost like a magnet to get the red blood cells to bind to the AllaQuix gauze and form a seal over the wound to stop bleeding.

A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.

description:
Absorbent Wound Care Dressing
This KerraMax Care absorbent wound dressing is constructed with a super-absorbent core that locks in and sequesters exudate, bacteria and MMPs away from the wound site to reduce the risk of maceration and promote faster, more effective healing. For added convenience, these medical dressings can be stacked to increase absorption when treating very wet wounds.

Comforting Protection
This non-adhesive wound dressing features a soft, non-woven material on both sides for a comfortable feel against the patient’s skin, along with excellent transpiration. Thanks to its unique absorbent core, this wound care treatment requires fewer changes and remains dry to the touch for improved patient comfort.

Leak-Free Flexibility
Designed with a unique horizontal wicking layer, KerraMax Care medical dressings are able to absorb exudate from a wound and distribute it throughout the dressing to prevent leaks. This absorbent wound dressing is also equipped with a heat-sealed border that works to prevent leakage while remaining soft and flexible.

Versatile Coverage
These absorbent and versatile primary or secondary medical dressings can be used to improve healing under all forms of compression. With the ability to absorb and retain large amounts of exudate, these dressings are a practical option for a variety of chronic and acute wound care treatments including diabetic wound care and venous leg ulcers. Easy to apply and remove, KerraMax Care Super Absorbent Wound Dressing can be comfortably used on toes, breasts, shoulders, elbows, hips, groin, heels and other parts of the body requiring absorbent wound care treatment.

A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.

Operating Guide:
1. Dip the bandage after unsealing into a basin of clean warm water of 25 degrees -30 degrees until the bubbles disappear and take out (about 5 seconds).
2. Dip only one roll of tape at a time, do not immerse the multi-roll bandage in the same pot at the same time.

A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.

What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.

The foam pad is non-adhesive (as long as wound has enough exudate to keep foam moist), and provides superior absorption, up to 60 ml of exudate, making it suitable for moderate to highly exudative wounds. It remains intact when saturated, may be removed in one-piece, and may be used in combination with other topicals. 2- BACKING LAYER: The thin, soft, breathable PU backing layer is reinforced with a white, non-woven Spunlace fabric mesh. 3- ADHESIVE LAYER: The wider than average adhesive border measures 1.2” all around the foam pad, and helps maintain the dressing in place as the absorbed exudates tend to weigh it down. The adhesive border should only be applied to normal, healthy skin around the wound. The combined backing and adhesive layer provide the water resistance capabilities: delaying the crossing of liquid from the outer surface into the dressing (about 10-20 minutes), breathable, and a decreased risk of wound and peri-wound maceration. A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.

What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

Absorbent Wound Care Dressing
This KerraMax Care absorbent wound dressing is constructed with a super-absorbent core that locks in and sequesters exudate, bacteria and MMPs away from the wound site to reduce the risk of maceration and promote faster, more effective healing. For added convenience, these medical dressings can be stacked to increase absorption when treating very wet wounds.

Comforting Protection
This non-adhesive wound dressing features a soft, non-woven material on both sides for a comfortable feel against the patient’s skin, along with excellent transpiration. Thanks to its unique absorbent core, this wound care treatment requires fewer changes and remains dry to the touch for improved patient comfort.

Leak-Free Flexibility
Designed with a unique horizontal wicking layer, KerraMax Care medical dressings are able to absorb exudate from a wound and distribute it throughout the dressing to prevent leaks. This absorbent wound dressing is also equipped with a heat-sealed border that works to prevent leakage while remaining soft and flexible.

Versatile Coverage
These absorbent and versatile primary or secondary medical dressings can be used to improve healing under all forms of compression. With the ability to absorb and retain large amounts of exudate, these dressings are a practical option for a variety of chronic and acute wound care treatments including diabetic wound care and venous leg ulcers. Easy to apply and remove, KerraMax Care Super Absorbent Wound Dressing can be comfortably used on toes, breasts, shoulders, elbows, hips, groin, heels and other parts of the body requiring absorbent wound care treatment.

What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

Self-adherent soft silicone dressing for scar care.

PRODUCT DESCRIPTION

Mepiform is a thin, discret and flexible dressing consisting of a laminate ( polyurethane and nonwoven) coverd with a soft silicone gel.

SAFETAC TECNOLOGY

Safetac is a patented soft silicone adhesive tecnology.

On the skin, a dressing with Safetac has gentle but secure adhesion with no epidermal stripping or pain on removal.

INTUDED USE

Mepiform is designed for the management of both old and new hypertrofhic and keloid scars.It can also be usedas a prophylactic therapy on closed wounds for prevention of hypertrophic or keloid scaring.

INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE
APLICATION

1. Open the packing and remove the dressing.

2. If necessary,cut to appropiate size alllowing overlap of minimum 1cm.

3. When applying Mepiform, make sure the area is dry.When used together with ointment or cream, ensure the dressing covers an area beyond the cream.

4. Remove the release film and apply mepiform over the scar / wound. Avoid stretching when applying over joints.

DRESSING CHANGE REMOVAL

1. Mepiform should optimally be worn for 24 hours a day. Remove the dressing once per a day for inspection and washing of the skin. The dressing can then be reapplied.

2. Mepiform should under normal conditions be changed every 3-7 days or when the adherent properties of the dressing are no longer sufficient.

3. Mepiform is waterproof and can be worn while bthing and showering.

AllaQuix is a sterile, topical, active hemostatic, wound dressing that is specifically designed to stop bleeding, even for people who normally have trouble stopping bleeding. HOW DOES ALLAQUIX WORK? AllaQuix works independent of the clotting cascade - which means AllaQuix will work whether the body is able to clot blood on its own or not. OPPOSITES ATTRACT! The chitosan fibers in AllaQuix have a positive charge. Red blood cells have a negative charge. Once the AllaQuix gauze is on the wound, the chitosan fibers in AllaQuix attract red blood cells. description:
Algisite M is a calcium-alginate dressing which forms a soft, integral gel when it comes into contact with wound exudate. Excess wound exudate is absorbed in this process. Algisite M utilises the proven benefits of moist wound healing, which results in faster healing of even difficult wounds. 

Features: 

■ Fast gelling, high mannuronic acid fibres 
■ Low fibre shed construction 
■ High integrity when wet 
■ Soft and conformable

Benefits 

Easy to remove 
When used in a moderate to highly exuding wound, the dressing forms a soft gel, which does not adhere to the delicate healing tissues in the wound bed. The dressing can be easily lifted out of the wound in one piece, or washed out with saline. 

Conforms to wound contours 
Algisite M is very soft and conformable, allowing it to be moulded, folded or cut to meet a wide range of wound shapes and sizes. As the fibres gel, an even more intimate contact with the wound is produced and maintained. 

Less fibre shed 
All fibre based alginates release fibres when handled, however the advanced bonding technique employed in Algisite M greatly reduces this. 

Moist wound environment 
The production of a gel by the action of exudate on the alginate fibres creates a moist wound environment at the wound surface. This prevents eschar formation and promotes faster healing. The dressing allows wound contraction to occur, which helps to reduce scarring and also allows gaseous exchange necessary for a healthy wound bed. 

Highly absorbent 
In vitro studies have shown that Algisite M can absorb 10 times its own weight in exudate. This allows the dressing to remain in the wound for up to 7 days, depending on the nature of the wound. 

Indications 

Full and partial thickness wounds, with moderate to heavy exudate which may also be prone to minor bleeding (e.g. pressure sores, leg ulcers, ischaemic and diabetic ulcers, post-operative wounds and fungating carcinomas.)

What is self-adhesive bandage?
A self-adhering bandage or cohesive bandage is a type of bandage or wrap that coheres to itself, but does not adhere well to other surfaces.
Because of this, it is commonly used as a wrap on limbs, since it will stick to itself and not loosen. It is used on humans, but also commonly used as a wrap on the legs of livestock because it will not stick to hair, so it is easily removed.

title: Tubular Bandage Applicator Size D (for Bulky Finger Dressings)
bullet_point: [Enables bandages to be applied quickly and easily]
description:
Application of a tubular bandage can sometimes be difficult and using an applicator can make the job a lot simpler, tidier, quicker and a lot less painful. Use a Plastic Applicator, Sugar Tong or Shuttlecock for sizes 00, 01 and 12 for fingers and toes, or a chrome cage for Elasticated Tubular Bandage or Gauze Stockinet for sizes C to F on adult ankles, wrists and limbs. Slide all of the measured tubular bandage onto the outside of the cage or applicator and slip the cage over the finger, toe or limb, pull off one end of the bandage at the bottom of the knuckle or joint and slide the cage over the area to cover, while releasing the bandage slowly, get to the end, twist around on a finger or just double back on yourself to then finish where you started. Cage can be slid off, leaving the bandage on the finger, toe or limb to be secured in place with a strip of sticky tape if required, while covering a dressing or compressing a swollen or painful joint without increased pain.

La aplicación de un vendaje tubular a veces puede ser difícil y usar un aplicador puede hacer el trabajo mucho más simple, ordenado, más rápido y mucho menos doloroso. overview
instructions for use
description
algisite #x25ca; m is a calcium-alginate dressing which forms a soft, gel that absorbs when it comes into contact with wound exudate. Algisite #x25ca; m helps utilize the proven benefits of moist wound management.
features
easy to remove

fast gelling, high mannuronic acid fibers
low fiber shed

soft and conformable
benefits
easy to remove
when used in a moderate to highly exuding wound, the dressing forms a soft gel, which does not adhere to the delicate healing tissues in the wound bed. The dressing can be easily lifted out of the wound in one piece, or washed out with saline.
conforms to wound contours
algisite #x25ca; m is very soft and conformable, allowing it to be molded, folded or cut to meet a wide range of wound shapes and sizes. As the fibers gel, an even more intimate contact with the wound is produced and maintained.
less fiber shed
all fiber based alginates release fibers when handled, however the advanced bonding technique employed in algisite #x25ca; m greatly reduces this.
moist wound environment
the production of a gel by the action of exudate on the alginate fibers creates a moist wound environment at the wound surface. This helps prevent eschar formation and promotes an optimal moist wound environment. The dressing allows wound contraction to occur, which may help reduce scarring and also allows gaseous exchange necessary for a healthy wound bed.
highly absorbent
in-vitro studies have shown that algisite #x25ca; m can absorb 13 times its own weight in exudate. This allows the dressing to remain in the wound for up to 7 days, depending on the nature of the wound and the volume of exudate
